symbols.name: vector space
symbols.meaning: The vector space on which the linear operator T acts.
symbols.quote: Here $U$ is a vector space and $T$ a linear operator on $U$.

symbols.name: eigenvalue
symbols.meaning: A scalar for which $Tv=\lambda v$ holds for some nonzero vector $v$ in $U$.
symbols.quote: A scalar $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $T$ when $Tv=\lambda v$ for some nonzero vector $v$ in $U$, and $v$ is then an eigenvector.

symbols.name: eigenvector
symbols.meaning: A nonzero vector $v$ in $U$ with $Tv=\lambda v$ for an eigenvalue $\lambda$, called an eigenvector.
symbols.quote: A scalar $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $T$ when $Tv=\lambda v$ for some nonzero vector $v$ in $U$, and $v$ is then an eigenvector.

symbols.name: coordinate count
symbols.meaning: The number of rational entries in each vector of $\mathbb{Q}^m$, at least 2.
symbols.quote: Here $\mathbb{Q}^m$ is the set of vectors with $m\ge2$ rational entries.

symbols.name: all-ones vector
symbols.meaning: The vector whose entries are all 1.
symbols.quote: Write $\mathbf 1$ for the all-ones vector, so the all-one matrix $J$ is $\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}$.

symbols.name: all-one matrix
symbols.meaning: The matrix with every entry 1, equal to $\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}$.
symbols.quote: Write $\mathbf 1$ for the all-ones vector, so the all-one matrix $J$ is $\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}$.

symbols.name: symmetric form matrix
symbols.meaning: A symmetric matrix whose form $x^{\mathsf T}Ay$ is tested for nondegeneracy.
symbols.quote: Eigenvalues test the nondegeneracy of a [symmetric matrix](symmetric-matrix.md) $A$.

symbols.name: average entry
symbols.meaning: The average entry of $x$, so that the part of $x$ along $\mathbf 1$ is $\gamma\mathbf 1$.
symbols.quote: Every $x\in\mathbb{Q}^m$ splits as $x=\gamma\mathbf 1+x_0$, where $\gamma$ is the average entry of $x$ and $x_0$ has entries summing to zero.

symbols.name: zero-sum part
symbols.meaning: The part of $x$ with entries summing to zero, so that $x=\gamma\mathbf 1+x_0$.
symbols.quote: Every $x\in\mathbb{Q}^m$ splits as $x=\gamma\mathbf 1+x_0$, where $\gamma$ is the average entry of $x$ and $x_0$ has entries summing to zero.
